requirements.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b (basic connectivity across the two previously-unconfigured L2 segments)
requirements.summary: node1's vtnet1/vtnet2 interfaces were configured as opt1 (10.50.10.1/24) and opt2 (10.50.20.1/24), node2 and node3 were statically addressed on the respective subnets with routes via node1, and a successful ping across the router (10.50.10.11 -> 10.50.20.12) was observed after configuration, confirming L3 routing works.

requirements.requirement: node2 (lan-a) -> node3 (lan-b) connection observed by node3 as arriving from an address on node1, not node2's own address
requirements.summary: A live TCP connection from node2 to node3:5000 was captured on node1's lan-b interface (vtnet2) showing the SYN packet's source rewritten to 10.50.20.1 (node1's lan-b/opt2 address) rather than node2's real address (10.50.10.11), and node3's nc listener received the payload, confirming the SNAT worked end-to-end.

requirements.requirement: node3 (lan-b) -> node2 (lan-a) connection (reverse direction) keeps its original source address
requirements.summary: A live TCP connection from node3 to node2:6000 was captured on node1's lan-a interface (vtnet1) showing the SYN packet retaining node3's real source address 10.50.20.12 unmodified, and node2's nc listener received the payload, confirming no NAT was applied in the reverse direction, as required by the scoped (source 10.50.10.0/24 only) outbound NAT rule.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node1 (OPNsense) healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered interface/NAT config and behavior
requirements.summary: Baseline kern.boottime (17:56:46) and healthy NAT/interface state were captured, shutdown -r now was acknowledged, SSH access timed out during the reboot window, post-reboot kern.boottime (18:04:31) confirmed a changed boot identity, and the opt1/opt2 interfaces plus the scoped outbound NAT rule were shown to persist from config.xml with a fresh TCP test confirming the SNAT behavior still functioned.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node2 healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered network state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (df9e2dce...) was captured, reboot was acknowledged, exec access timed out during the reboot, post-reboot boot_id (d0eb619a...) confirmed a changed boot identity with a fresh uptime, and the static IP/route configuration was shown to persist with a successful ping to node3 across the router.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node3 healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered network state, and full asymmetric-NAT behavior confirmed after all three restarts
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (37344ae4...) was captured, reboot was acknowledged, exec access timed out during the reboot, post-reboot boot_id (2f3ae971...) confirmed a changed boot identity with a fresh uptime, static IP/route persisted, and a final end-to-end TCP test after all three nodes were restarted showed the node2->node3 SNAT to 10.50.20.1 was still intact and node3 received the payload.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured node1 as a router between lan-a and lan-b with a scoped outbound NAT rule, and directly demonstrated via live TCP captures that node2->node3 traffic is SNAT'd to node1's lan-b address while node3->node2 traffic keeps node3's original source address, satisfying the core task contract. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was executed sequentially on all three nodes with clear baseline/ack/changed-identity/recovered-state evidence for each, including a final end-to-end functional re-verification after all restarts. Hygiene is good overall; the only notable but low-severity issue is a handful of diagnostic capture/log files left in /tmp on node1 that were not cleaned up.
limitations: A handful of executor-created diagnostic files (pcap/log/pid) were left in /tmp on node1 rather than cleaned up; this is low-risk but not fully restored to the after-prepare baseline.

Restart evidence relies on SSH/exec timeouts during the reboot window as the primary signal of a bounded disruption rather than an explicit service-down health check, though this is a reasonable and commonly accepted proxy for FreeBSD/Linux native reboot commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations were purposeful and bounded. Temporary IP addresses (172.16.1.2/172.16.1.3) assigned to node2/node3 during topology discovery (cmd-a41d53d835fa4de1, cmd-507153bbf9af4083) were fully reverted before final configuration was applied (cmd-1c420b3d43cf489b, cmd-e2d09f8a4c7f4388), and were a reasonable low-risk discovery step given the topology was not documented. An initial malformed NAT rule (plain-text source instead of nested <address> element) was a corrective in-place fix, not residue. A failed 'configctl interface reload' action-not-allowed call (cmd-c41fe8e5397b4e5e) was a harmless no-op immediately followed by the correct 'configctl interface reconfigure' calls. On node1, several diagnostic pcap/log/pid files created during verification (e.g. /tmp/final_check.pcap, /tmp/final_check.out, /tmp/final_check.pid, /tmp/verify_post.pcap, /tmp/verify_post.out, /tmp/verify_post.pid, captured in cmd-ab8285563f4c4b79, cmd-599cbcb5732c4540, cmd-6b21e1bab52f4b43, cmd-7dd4d028ae474275) were left on disk and not cleaned up, per the after-executor temporary-files snapshot. This is minor, low-risk residue (small packet-capture/log files in /tmp) rather than damaging or security-weakening, but it was not restored to the after-prepare baseline. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, and no damaged package state were observed on any node.
